draft.title: The Weimar Republic
card: The Weimar Republic was Germany's democracy from 1919 to 1933. It began after Germany lost the First World War and the Kaiser gave up the throne.
It was weak from the start. Many Germans blamed the new government for the Treaty of Versailles, and there were uprisings from the extreme left and right.
In 1923 hyperinflation made money almost worthless and wiped out the savings of many families. Later, a period of recovery in the mid 1920s was helped by American loans.
The Great Depression after 1929 ended the American loans and raised unemployment sharply. Support for extreme parties, including the Nazis, grew, and in 1933 the Nazis ended the republic.
draft.remember: Weimar was a democracy born in defeat, shaken by crises, and ended when the Depression helped the Nazis rise.

a.q: Why did many Germans distrust the Weimar Republic from its early years?
opts: They blamed it for the defeat and the Treaty of Versailles
They believed it had started the First World War
They thought it gave too much power to the Kaiser
They saw it as too slow to join the Allied powers
a.why: The republic took power as Germany lost the war, so many people blamed it for the defeat and the Treaty of Versailles. It did not start the war, and the Kaiser had already gone.
a.clue: Think about who was in government when the war ended.

b.q: Karl, a clerk in Hamburg, says the republic was safe in 1927 but in danger by 1932. Which event best explains the change?
opts: The Depression ended American loans and raised unemployment
Hyperinflation destroyed the value of German money
An uprising removed the Kaiser from power
The Treaty of Versailles was signed that year
b.why: The Depression ended the American loans that had helped the recovery and raised unemployment, so extreme parties gained support. Hyperinflation is a tempting answer, but it happened in 1923, before the stable years Karl describes.

a.best: They blamed it for the defeat and the Treaty of Versailles

b.best: The Depression ended American loans and raised unemployment

problems.detail: The option 'The Treaty of Versailles was signed that year' does not say which year 'that year' is (1927 or 1932), so the distractor is confusing as written.
